newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen. Roth introduces bill for inflation board.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen. Roth introduces bill for inflation board.

text.p: The top Republican and Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee have introduced legislation to create a board to help improve the accuracy of measuring inflation, a committee spokeswoman said Wednesday.

The legislation, introduced late Tuesday, would create a Cost of Living Board to "improve our government's ability to index federal programs with a more accurate measure of inflation," Roth said in his floor statement Tuesday.
The five-member board would review statistical evidence about inflation and then produce a cost of living adjustment by Nov. 1 each year, he said.

The inflation adjustment number would be the one to which federal benefit programs and tax items would be indexed for the coming year, without further action by the Congress or the President, Roth, a Delaware Republican, said.
If the board failed by a majority vote to produce a cost of living adjustment, then current law would apply which uses the consumer price index to index the programs.
The aim of the board was not to study the accuracy of the CPI, Roth said.
An advisory commission late last year said the CPI overstated inflation by about 1.1 percentage points a year.
